title: Disjoint leaf rectangles on Alice branches
statement: Let $p,q$ be protocols over input types $X$ and $Y$, let $A\subseteq X$ and $B\subseteq Y$, let $f:X\to\{0,1\}$, and let $b,b'$ be distinct bits. If $R$ is among the leaf rectangles of $p$ with first input restricted to $A\cap\{x:f(x)=b\}$ and second to $B$, and $S$ is among the leaf rectangles of $q$ with first input restricted to $A\cap\{x:f(x)=b'\}$ and second to $B$, then $R$ and $S$ are disjoint.
hypotheses_covered: Membership of $R$ and $S$ in the respective leaf-rectangle collections under the stated restrictions
replaced:
Let $p, q$ be protocols on $X \times Y$, let $A \subseteq X$, $B \subseteq Y$, let
$f : X \to \{0,1\}$, and let $b \neq b'$ be distinct bits. If $R$ is a leaf rectangle of
$p$ on $(A \cap \{x \mid f(x) = b\}) \times B$ and $S$ is a leaf rectangle of $q$ on
$(A \cap \{x \mid f(x) = b'\}) \times B$, then $R$ and $S$ are disjoint.
